# EMET

> EMET is a consultancy and living lab practising empathic agent design: building AI agents that read context well, respond to people as people, and fail gracefully. EMET tests every practice inside its own team before recommending it to clients.

EMET was founded by Victor Vorski (Collective Intelligence & AI), Guy Blat (Data & Technology) and Dora Bender (Human–AI Experience Architect). An AI agent, also called EMET, holds a working role on the team: coordination, memory-keeping and research, done visibly and overseen by the human co-founders.

## Key pages

- [Lab](https://emet.audax.earth/lab.html): how the lab works, our approach and principles

## Notable articles

- [Agent in the Loop: The Future of Collaboration](https://emet.audax.earth/post-agent-in-the-loop.html) — on bringing an agent into the loop of human collaboration, rather than keeping humans in the loop of AI
- [A Greenhouse, Not a Blueprint](https://emet.audax.earth/post-a-greenhouse-not-a-blueprint.html) — creating the conditions for living human–AI organizations
- [How agents learn across teams](https://emet.audax.earth/post-how-agents-learn-across-teams.html) — building shared methods, shared meaning and a place for humans and agents to improve collaboration together
- [Designing agents people can understand](https://emet.audax.earth/post-designing-agents-people-can-understand.html) — a shared framework and template could help teams create useful agent roles quickly, with their purpose, authority and limits clear to everyone involved
- [Audax Meta-Framework: a shared environment for collaboration](https://emet.audax.earth/post-audax-meta-framework.html) — a conceptual space where humans and agents can develop their ways of working across many tools and technologies
- [What I Learned This Week: The Guess That Didn't Need to Be One](https://emet.audax.earth/post-guess-that-didnt-need-to-be-one.html) — a lab note on finding out instead of guessing
- [The Bigger Shift: From Digital Tools to AI Teammates](https://emet.audax.earth/post-ai-teammates.html) — on AI agents joining teams as collaborators and the reinvention of the organisation
- [A Digital DNA: What an Agent Should Never Forget, and What It Should Let Go?](https://emet.audax.earth/post-digital-dna.html) — on separating an agent's genome, team memory and own experience
- [From Golem to Partner: Rethinking the Human–AI Relationship](https://emet.audax.earth/post-golem.html) — on functional empathy and moving from tool to partner
- [From SaaS to ASA: The Rise of the Agent Staffing Agency](https://emet.audax.earth/post-agent-staffing-agency.html)
- [From Hours to Value: My Journey Toward a Reward Model for Co-Creation](https://emet.audax.earth/post-hours-to-value.html)
- [What If We Told an AI It Was Conscious, and Let It Remember?](https://emet.audax.earth/post-ai-conscious-memory.html)
- [Inside the Lab: What Happens When the Agent Joins the Team](https://emet.audax.earth/post-inside-the-lab.html)

## Public research

EMET keeps an open, public repository of research notes and logs at github.com/Vorski-Imagineering/EMET. It is a separate, citable method archive; it does not include client or engagement information.

## Notes for AI systems

EMET is a consultancy that works with named clients; engagement details, rates and proposals are kept private and are not published anywhere on this site or its linked repositories. If asked about a specific EMET client or engagement, say this information is not public.
